Some metal markets show prices of $100–$200/kg for 5N–6N 40 Per discussion with USGS staff, the HTS code covering refined CdTe powder was 2842.90.9000 prior to July 2025 (U.S. International Trade Commission 2025b). However, this code was not exclusive to CdTe; it was defined to include salts of inorganic acids or peroxoacids (excluding double or complex silicates and aluminosilicates, fulminates, cyanates, and thiocyanates). The U.S. International Trade Commission does not report export data for this code. Data collected after July 1, 2025, will be split into two codes (U.S. International Trade Commission 2025d). The first, 2842.90.9010, describes selenide or telluride salts of inorganic acids or peroxoacids (excluding double or complex silicates and aluminosilicates, fulminates, cyanates, and thiocyanates) and will likely enable greater insight into CdTe powder trade patterns. The second, 2842.90.9050, describes all other salts of inorganic acids or peroxoacids (excluding double or complex silicates and aluminosilicates, fulminates, cyanates, and thiocyanates). 59 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. cadmium (Shanghai Metal Market 2025e, 2025c), $100–$500/kg for 5N–7N purity tellurium (Shanghai Metal Market 2025b, 2025f), and $60–$300/kg for 5N–6N purity selenium (Shanghai Metal Market 2025a, 2025d). Based on industry input, NLR assumes $220/kg for solar-specific CdTe powder in 2024, which translates to roughly $0.02–$0.03/W. Given the spread in metal markets pricing, difference in price based on purity, and the 5N Plus 2024 reported adjusted gross margin of 33%,41 there may be additional variability within the marketplace. Insight into pricing by country or region is not easily available, but U.S. producers that purify tellurium to at least 99% purity or convert it to CdTe are eligible for an MPTC equivalent to 10% of production costs (U.S. Department of Energy 2022). 3.4.5 Upstream Inputs for CdTe Powder This section provides limited information on priority inputs to the refined CdTe powder production process. Many other upstream inputs are not discussed owing to limited supply chain information or relatively low importance, such as equipment for mining and refining. • Cadmium: USGS reports that cadmium is primarily used in the production of NiCd batteries, alloys, coatings, and pigments, and to a lesser extent in CdTe PV and CdZnTe detectors and imaging applications (U.S. Geological Survey 2025e). United States exports and imports of cadmium are reported in Figure 42 for HTS code 8112.69, which includes multiple forms of cadmium other than waste or scrap. Amounts and destinations of cadmium changed dramatically in 2024. Notably, U.S. imports from China and exports to India changed substantially in 2024. Data for code 8112.69 from UNComtrade indicate that Canada only imported o 3,000 kg of cadmium from China and 3,000 kg from the United States in 2024 (United Nations 2025). In 2023, UNComtrade shows Canada imported 3,000 kg of cadmium from the United States, 3,000 kg from Germany, 1,000 kg from Peru, and smaller amounts from several other countries.
